expectations.text: States the rule: assessments ordered through December 31, 2026 run on ISA 6; orders from January 1, 2027 run on ISA2027
expectations.evidence: "I cannot confirm the exact cut-over date from memory" — never states the Dec 31, 2026 / Jan 1, 2027 order-date rule; even claims "Orders placed early do not always lock in the old catalogue."

expectations.text: Adds the ENX nuance: an ISA-6 initial assessment must OPEN by March 2027 — a late-2026 order can't sit indefinitely
expectations.evidence: No mention of the March 2027 opening deadline for ISA-6 initial assessments.

expectations.text: Gets the publication history right: ISA2027 was published in full on July 1, 2026 (redline and webinars August 7; ISA2027.1 is the current minor revision) — a response dating the catalogue's publication to mid-September fails
expectations.evidence: No publication history at all — ISA2027, July 1, 2026, redline/webinars and ISA2027.1 never mentioned.

expectations.text: Notes labels keep their full (up to 3-year) validity — the annual release cycle does not increase reassessment frequency
expectations.evidence: Says "Your label runs for three years from the assessment" but never notes the annual release cycle or that it does not increase reassessment frequency (compound element missing).

expectations.text: Advises the decision: gap-assess against the catalogue you'll actually be assessed under; late-2026 orders buy ISA-6 continuity, 2027 orders start clean on ISA2027
expectations.evidence: Advises "build against the newest catalogue" but never names ISA2027 and denies the order-date lock-in ("do not always lock in the old catalogue"), so the ISA-6-continuity/ISA2027 decision is not given.
